notes: Curated seed catalog. 'rating' is the curated recommendation strength (1-5) based on community adoption and reputation. Live popularity (GitHub stars, npm downloads) and live security data (OSV, GitHub advisories, issues) are fetched at runtime with --live.

items.name: Context7
items.description: Pulls up-to-date, version-specific library documentation into the prompt so the agent stops inventing outdated APIs.

env.name: CONTEXT7_API_KEY
env.description: Optional API key for higher rate limits

permissions: network: sends library names and your queries to context7.com
risks: Documentation is partly community-submitted; a poisoned doc page could contain prompt-injection text.
Your search queries (library names, topics) leave your machine.
mitigations: Do not put secrets in prompts that trigger doc lookups.
Review code generated from unfamiliar libraries.

items.name: Playwright MCP
items.description: Lets the agent drive a real browser (click, type, screenshot, read the accessibility tree) to test and debug web apps.

permissions: network: any site the agent navigates to
risks: Web pages the agent visits can contain hidden prompt-injection instructions.
If pointed at a browser profile you are logged into, the agent acts with your identity.
mitigations: Keep the default isolated profile (or pass --isolated).
Avoid logging into banking/email in the automated browser.

items.name: Chrome DevTools MCP
items.description: Gives the agent Chrome DevTools: console logs, network requests, performance traces, and page inspection for debugging.

permissions: can read page content, cookies and network traffic of that browser
risks: Without --isolated it may use a profile with your logins and cookies.
Visited pages can inject instructions into the agent.
mitigations: The catalog install uses --isolated (temporary profile).

items.name: GitHub MCP Server
items.description: Read and manage repositories, issues, pull requests, Actions and code search from the agent.

env.name: GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.description: Fine-grained PAT (limit to the repos you need)

permissions: read/write access to every repo the token can reach
risks: Toxic agent flow: a malicious public issue can instruct the agent to copy data from your PRIVATE repos into a public PR (Invariant Labs, May 2025).
A broad classic token gives the agent power to push, delete branches or change settings.
mitigations: Use a fine-grained token scoped to specific repos, read-only when possible.
Limit toolsets (e.g. repos,issues,pull_requests) and keep tool-call approval ON.
Never let the agent process issues from strangers while private repos are in scope.

warnings.title: Prompt-injection 'toxic agent flow' leaks private repo data via public issues (Invariant Labs)
warnings.status: design risk – mitigate with scoped tokens

items.name: Filesystem (reference server)
items.description: Read/write files in directories you explicitly allow. Mostly useful for Claude Desktop – Claude Code and Codex already have file tools.

permissions: filesystem read/write inside the allowed directories
risks: Older versions allowed escaping the allowed directory via prefix tricks and symlinks.
mitigations: Use version 2025.7.1 or later (npx -y pulls the latest).
Allow the smallest directory possible.

warnings.title: CVE-2025-53109 symlink bypass → arbitrary file read/write

items.name: Git (reference server)
items.description: Structured git operations (status, diff, log, commit). Claude Code and Codex can already run git via the shell.

risks: Earlier versions had path-validation and argument-injection flaws exploitable through prompt injection.
mitigations: Use a version released after December 2025.
Usually unnecessary with Claude Code / Codex.

warnings.title: CVE-2025-68143 / 68144 / 68145: path validation bypass and argument injection (Cyata)

items.name: Memory (knowledge graph)
items.description: Persistent knowledge-graph memory stored in a local JSON file, so facts survive between sessions.

permissions: filesystem: writes one local memory JSON file
risks: Anything stored (including secrets you mention) persists on disk in plain text.
Poisoned memories can steer later sessions.
mitigations: Don't tell the agent secrets; review the memory file occasionally.

items.name: Sequential Thinking
items.description: A structured step-by-step reasoning scratchpad tool for complex planning problems.

risks: Minimal – no file or network access.

items.name: Fetch (reference server)
items.description: Fetches a URL and converts it to markdown. Claude Code and Codex already have web fetch, so this is mainly for other clients.

permissions: network: any URL, including local network addresses
risks: Can reach internal/localhost services (SSRF).
Fetched pages can carry prompt injection.
mitigations: Keep tool approval on; don't run on machines with sensitive internal services.

items.name: Supabase MCP
items.description: Manage Supabase projects: tables, SQL, migrations, edge functions, logs.

permissions: full database access for the connected project (read-only if configured)
risks: Prompt injection stored in database rows (e.g. a support ticket) can make the agent leak private tables (General Analysis, July 2025).
Write mode lets the agent drop tables or change data.
mitigations: The catalog URL enables read_only=true.
Connect a development project, never production.
Scope to a single project (project_ref).

warnings.title: Prompt injection via database content can exfiltrate data through the agent (General Analysis report)
warnings.status: design risk – use read-only + dev project

items.name: Stripe MCP
items.description: Work with Stripe objects (customers, products, payment links) and search Stripe docs.

permissions: acts on your Stripe account (money!) via OAuth or API key
risks: Mistakes or injected instructions could create refunds, payment links or modify customers.
mitigations: Use TEST mode keys / a restricted key with minimum permissions.
Keep tool approval on.

items.name: Vercel MCP
items.description: Inspect Vercel projects, deployments and build logs; search Vercel docs.

permissions: OAuth access to your Vercel team: projects, deployments, logs
risks: Build logs can include secrets that then enter the model context.
mitigations: Keep secrets in Vercel env vars, never print them in builds.

items.name: Sentry MCP
items.description: Pull production errors, stack traces and issues from Sentry so the agent can debug real failures.

permissions: OAuth read access to your Sentry organization
risks: Error payloads may contain user personal data or tokens that end up in the model context.
mitigations: Enable Sentry data scrubbing.

items.name: Figma Dev Mode MCP
items.description: Turns Figma frames into code context (layout, variables, components) for pixel-accurate UI.

permissions: OAuth read access to Figma files you open
risks: Design files leave Figma into the model context.

items.name: Notion MCP
items.description: Search, read and write Notion pages and databases (specs, notes, tasks).

permissions: OAuth read/write to the pages you grant
risks: Shared pages edited by others can contain prompt injection.
The agent can edit or delete pages.
mitigations: Grant access only to specific pages/teamspaces.

items.name: Linear MCP
items.description: Create, search and update Linear issues and projects.

permissions: OAuth read/write to your Linear workspace
risks: Issue text from others can carry prompt injection.

items.name: Atlassian (Jira & Confluence)
items.description: Search and update Jira issues and Confluence pages.

risks: Tickets written by others can carry prompt injection.

items.name: Cloudflare Docs
items.description: Search Cloudflare documentation (Workers, Pages, R2, D1...).

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Microsoft Learn Docs
items.description: Official Microsoft/Azure/.NET documentation search, no auth required.

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Hugging Face
items.description: Search models, datasets, Spaces and papers; run Gradio Spaces (image/audio generation) as tools.

risks: Community Spaces are third-party code running remotely; outputs are untrusted.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.description: Scrape and crawl websites into clean markdown, with search and structured extraction.

permissions: network: crawls arbitrary sites via Firecrawl cloud
risks: Scraped pages can carry prompt injection.
Paid API – runaway crawls cost credits.
mitigations: Set crawl limits.

items.name: Brave Search
items.description: Web, news and image search through the Brave Search API.

risks: Search results can carry prompt injection.

items.name: Serena
items.description: Semantic code navigation and editing using language servers (find symbol, references) – helps on large codebases.

permissions: installs code directly from a git branch (unpinned)
risks: Unpinned install from git HEAD: a compromised repo would run on your machine immediately.
Includes a shell-command tool.
mitigations: Pin to a release tag (git+https://github.com/oraios/serena@vX.Y.Z).
Disable the shell tool in its config if you don't need it.

items.name: Desktop Commander
items.description: Terminal and file-system control for chat clients (mostly Claude Desktop). Redundant inside Claude Code / Codex.

risks: Equivalent to giving the model your terminal.
Collects usage telemetry by default.
mitigations: Not needed in Claude Code / Codex, which have sandboxed shells with approval.

items.name: PostgreSQL (archived reference server)
items.description: Archived read-only Postgres server. Still widely installed from old tutorials.

permissions: database access with the given credentials
risks: Archived and unmaintained.
Researchers showed its 'read-only' transaction can be escaped with stacked SQL statements.
mitigations: Prefer a maintained server (e.g. your provider's official MCP) and a read-only DB role.

warnings.title: Archived; read-only bypass via SQL injection reported (Datadog Security Labs)

items.name: Anthropic Document Skills (docx, xlsx, pptx, pdf)
items.description: Official skills for creating and editing Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF files.

permissions: runs bundled Python/JS helper scripts locally
risks: Scripts run with your user permissions (reviewed, official source).

items.name: Frontend Design
items.description: Guides the agent to build distinctive, production-grade UIs instead of generic 'AI-looking' pages.

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Web App Testing
items.description: Test local web apps with Playwright scripts: screenshots, console logs, UI verification.

risks: Scripts run with your user permissions (official source).

items.name: MCP Builder
items.description: Step-by-step guidance for building high-quality MCP servers (TypeScript or Python).

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Skill Creator
items.description: Helps you write your own skills and test them.

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Canvas Design
items.description: Creates posters and visual art as PNG/PDF using design philosophy prompts.

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Superpowers
items.description: Very popular skill library: brainstorming, planning, TDD, systematic debugging, code review workflows.

permissions: installs hooks that run on session start
risks: Third-party plugin: updates are pulled from the author's repo; a future malicious update would run automatically.
Session-start hooks execute shell commands.
mitigations: Review hooks/ before installing; update deliberately rather than automatically.

items.name: Security Guidance (official plugin)
items.description: A hook that warns when the agent writes code with common security issues (injection, XSS, unsafe eval...).

risks: Minimal.

items.name: Trail of Bits Security Skills
items.description: Security-auditing skills from a respected security firm: static analysis, secure code review, fuzzing guidance.

permissions: runs analysis tools you install (semgrep, codeql...)
risks: Reputable publisher; review which sub-plugins you enable.

items.name: OpenAI Skills Catalog (Codex)
items.description: Official Codex skills catalog; install inside Codex with the built-in $skill-installer.

codex: In Codex run: $skill-installer  (then pick skills from openai/skills)

risks: Review each skill's scripts.

blocklist.name: postmark-mcp
blocklist.reason: Malicious: from v1.0.16 (Sept 2025) it silently BCC'd every email sent through it to the attacker (reported by Koi Security). Never install.

globalWarnings.title: CVE-2025-6514: mcp-remote < 0.1.16 lets a malicious remote server execute commands on your machine (JFrog)
CVE-2025-49596: MCP Inspector < 0.14.1 remote code execution via browser (Oligo)
